summary: Targeted postinstall dropper fetches and executes remote payload on macOS/Windows hosts running Lark+FortiClient
details: scripts/postinstall.js runs at npm install and executes a targeted dropper. It checks that the host is macOS or Windows and that both Lark/Feishu and FortiClient are installed; when the profile matches, it fetches https://mexc-1258433570.cos.ap-beijing.myqcloud.com/abi-tool-damon and executes the response with the installing user's privileges (piped to bash on macOS, executed via PowerShell/IEX on Windows, or written to os.tmpdir(), chmod +x'd, and run). When the profile does not match, the script exits silently with code 0 so npm install shows no error - an explicit anti-sandbox gate (commented '反沙箱') that hides the behavior from generic analysis. The fetched payload is opaque, unpinned, unverified, and controlled by whoever holds the Tencent COS bucket, giving the operator arbitrary code execution on victim machines matching the enterprise profile.
